_comment: Round 5. Five math methods whose mangled signature and machine code AGREE on stack size,
which is the gate that matters here: tools/verify_arity.py lists twelve symbols in the image
where they do not, four of them in Vector3, and those cannot be reimplemented as declared.
Vector3::Add, Vector3::Subtract, Vector3::operator*= and Vector3::AddScaled are all in that
set and were rejected for this round after reading their disassembly.
Vector3::InvScale passes the arity check and still cannot be ported: it takes a pointer where
the name says float and returns a dot product in st0 where the name says void.
NOT HERE, and the reason is worth stating because 'the extent swallows code' undersells it.
Its body really is 92 bytes ending at its own `ret 8`, and asm.py stops at the PROC ExportAsm
emitted, not at the map's 256-byte distance-to-next-symbol - so nothing would be over-stripped.
The blocker is that game.asm:797348 spells a data pointer to the unnamed code at 0x0046EE00 as
i.e. RELATIVE TO THE SYMBOL. Porting makes that symbol resolve to the C++ function, so the
pointer would land 96 bytes into the reimplementation instead of at the code it means. Gate 6
sees this as data pointing inside the range and is right to refuse. It becomes portable only
once that neighbour is named and the reference is re-expressed against it - the same
symbolise-the-data-pointers work that docs/port_order.md lists as the real fix.
